comments.author: Javascript
comments.message: Image mirror requested by ppl: Spoiler The chest name explanation: Spoiler The phrase “Merin sa haryalyë alassë!” comes from Quenya, one of the Elvish languages created by J.R.R. Tolkien. It can be broken down as follows: merin means “I wish” or “I want,” sa means “that,” haryalyë means “you have” (from harya- “to have” with the pronoun ending -lyë for “you”), and alassë means “joy” or “happiness.” Therefore, the phrase literally translates to “I wish that you have joy.” In natural English, this would be expressed as “I wish you joy.” It’s a kind and poetic way of offering someone happiness or blessing them with joy, fitting the gentle and musical tone of Tolkien’s Elvish languages. This rare collectible chest with unique items was obtained during the New Year 2025 event. It’s in perfect condition and has never been opened! It can be mailed or traded in person near the portal. comments.author: Vamashi
comments.message: Sniper protection: optional. When bidding gets fast paced and heated toward the end of the auction, sniper protection will extend the auction by a set time after the last bid. For example, if there are 2 minutes left in the auction, with a 1-hour sniper protection, and someone places a new high bid, the auction is extended by 1 hour. If another bid comes in after that, the auction is extended again by 1 hour from the time of the bid, and so on, until there are no more bids within an hour of the last one. comments.author: Davih
comments.message: 7 minutes ago, jotasiete said: I'm just auctioning his boat - he's a player and the one who asked me to handle the auction process. That's all. Please consider that changing the ownership of a boat is possible, and it's pretty much expected when doing this kind of trades. The owner will have to "change owner" to the one who actually bought it, so that He can have full permissions and use it normally. Otherwise buying it would be a complete waste of time and money, so saying things like "ownership is immortalized" might confuse and scare away customers, even if it's probably AI-written stuff. I think the seller is is good faith, just confused about game mechanics, I've seen Andreum as an active player (today) at the slay, and I think that he is part of their group. comments.author: Kinganon
comments.message: Supreme items are priced for their ability to keep enchantments for twice as long as rare items, and 10 times longer than common items. In addition, they take less damage from use, lose significantly less QL when repaired, and reduce all action timers by 0.2 seconds. For gathering tools like the shovel, the rarity affects the QL ceiling of all items dug, allowing you to dig items at a higher level than your skill level. This effect can be combined with the harvesting rune to push your max QL even higher. For the high-level diggers out there, here's your chance to finally up your game. Good luck! Edited March 30, 2024 by Kinganon Closing

comments.message: Sniper protection extends the auction. Sniper protection: optional. When bidding gets fast paced and heated toward the end of the auction, sniper protection will extend the auction by a set time after the last bid. For example, if there are 2 minutes left in the auction, with a 1-hour sniper protection, and someone places a new high bid, the auction is extended by 1 hour. If another bid comes in after that, the auction is extended again by 1 hour from the time of the bid, and so on, until there are no more bids within an hour of the last one. The sniper protection time frame may be set to any number, though should be kept reasonable

comments.author: Eridil
comments.message: Dear Community Members, I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to share some recent developments that may be of interest to those considering land acquisitions or collaborative endeavors on the Cadence server of Wurm Online. Recently, I entered into a surface mining contract with two individuals, Theoldguy and Spellmizer. While the initial stages of our collaboration were productive, an unexpected situation arose that necessitated a reassessment of our agreement. Spellmizer, one of the contractors, proceeded to deed land strategically located between my deed and that of an allied party. This action, not discussed or agreed upon within the scope of our contract, took me and my villagers by surprise. Given the nature of this action, which was perceived as potentially hostile, it led to discomfort and concern among my villagers and subsequently, the cancellation of the ongoing contract. I believe it is important to maintain transparency in our community, especially concerning land dealings and partnerships. Therefore, I feel obliged to inform potential bidders and interested parties about this incident. While I refrain from casting aspersions on the characters of Theoldguy and Spellmizer, I advise caution. Any future dealings or land acquisitions in this area might inadvertently involve you in complexities or disagreements stemming from the actions of these individuals. I urge those interested in this matter to consider all aspects carefully and to approach any agreements or transactions with informed caution. It is always beneficial to communicate openly and establish clear, mutually agreed-upon terms before entering into any contract or land purchase. Thank you for taking the time to read this notice. If there are any questions or if further discussion is desired, please feel free to reach out to me. Best Regards, NFI Trison SFI Eridil

comments.author: Eridil
comments.message: Dear Community Members, I would like to clarify a point regarding the recent developments on the Cadence server. At no point did I assert that the actions undertaken by Spellmizer and Theoldguy were against the game's rules. However, it is widely regarded within our community as poor form to initiate a deed under the circumstances described, especially while under contract. The crux of the issue, as I see it, is not about rule-breaking but about the underlying intentions and ethics of gameplay. The actions of these players seem driven not by a desire to build or be good neighbors, but rather by what appears to be sheer greed. They have every right to auction their land, but as a member of this community, I also reserve the right to inform potential buyers about the nature of this deed and the character of those they are dealing with. I would urge prospective buyers to critically assess the value of this land. My contentions are: 1. Value Assessment: The land in question, as marketed, may not possess the value or resources claimed. Many of the nodes mentioned are not even within the protected boundaries of the deed. In fact, these resources are being utilized by my villagers as per their needs, a testament to the accessibility of these resources to anyone in the area. 2. Community Relations: Purchasing this disputed land could lead to challenging dynamics with the local community, including my villagers. The history of the deed and the manner in which it was acquired could complicate future interactions and collaborations. 3. Ethical Considerations: Engaging in business with individuals who have demonstrated questionable practices should be a decision made with caution. The way this situation has unfolded raises concerns about trust and integrity, essential in any transaction or partnership. 4. Misrepresentation of Proximity: Contrary to Spellmizer's claims, his deed is not situated 30 tiles away from my own, but rather, it is directly adjacent to my deed's perimeter. This misrepresentation of facts is a critical concern for potential buyers, as it directly impacts the context and potential conflicts regarding this land. 5. Limited Expansion Opportunities: Prospective buyers should also be aware that the potential for expanding this deed is considerably limited. Its placement, right alongside the perimeter of an existing deed and blocked by several structures belonging to my neighbor, severely restricts any meaningful expansion. This significantly impacts the long-term viability and development potential of the land. In conclusion, while transactions and game-play strategies like this are a part of Wurm Online, it's also important to consider the broader impact of such actions on the community and individual gaming experience. I encourage all potential buyers and partners to weigh these factors carefully before making a decision. Thank you for considering this perspective. Edited November 18, 2023 by Eridil

comments.author: ShaunChadwick
comments.message: Sniper protection: optional. When bidding gets fast paced and heated toward the end of the auction, sniper protection will extend the auction by a set time after the last bid. For example, if there are 2 minutes left in the auction, with a 1-hour sniper protection, and someone places a new high bid, the auction is extended by 1 hour. If another bid comes in after that, the auction is extended again by 1 hour from the time of the bid, and so on, until there are no more bids within an hour of the last one. The sniper protection time frame may be set to any number, though should be kept reasonable.

comments.message: Then I'll be the one to tell you of one of your mistakes: not having a sniper protection. If someone bids, the auction ends no less than the sniper protection time after said bid. For example: someone bids at :14 on an auction with 30min sniper protection. The auction was supposed to end :20 so the bid was still 6 minutes before end. However, the auction now ends 30 minutes after the last bid (at :44) and will keep being extended by further bids until 30 minutes after the last bid has passed. The purpose is as the obvious name suggests, to protect from people sniping with a bid last second. Almost no auctions run without snipe protection for a damn good reason. My first bid was 1s, my reserve is probably much lower than the going price, but you do you I also won't bid on an item that has a hidden reserve. My reason is that when the auction is over, the seller can simply state that the reserve was never reached and thus there is no sale. I'm not wasting my time bidding or watching an auction when this is possible. For me, the general idea is, if you want a certain price for something...thus your hidden reserve, then start the bidding at that point and see where it goes. The ONLY time I would bid on a hidden reserve auction is if I have built some kind of relationship over time with the seller and I have a high level of trust in them. Good luck with your auction and Happy Wurming!

comments.author: Glynflorel
comments.message: A cute little horse with a rare draft trait. Since I haven’t seen these being traded publicly yet, I decided to try my hand at an auction. Starting bid: 15 s Increment (minimum): 1 s Sniper Protection: 1 hour Private Bids: not acceptedPick-up at Melody N13 (reachable by boat).

comments.author: Aleck
comments.message: I'd love to buy this horse, but the price is a bit too steep with how difficult (suspected impossible) it is for the rare horse traits to be passed to offspring, and the horse having only 2 draft traits otherwise. Would you consider auctioning at a lower start value and/or a private sale, assuming someone doesn't prove me wrong and bid?

comments.author: Sinnjinn
comments.message: I thought I read in the update notes that the rare traits are not passed. But I could be wrong. But if that is true, 15s is crazy IMHO

comments.author: Glynflorel
comments.message: Hi Aleck, I completely understand the hesitation! From my own observations, I’m guesstimating that the trait has a 10% chance of passing on if a single parent has it. (Based on a rather small sample size of approximately 15 breedings with the trait passing twice, at approximately 65 AH.) Admittingly for a female that still means it is likely to take a long time before the trait passes. On the other hand, that is still significantly better than the random chance of getting the trait, and I may essentially be giving up on a monopoly on the trait by selling her. (It’s unclear to me if anyone else has managed to breed it yet - I was in part hoping this auction might reveal that.) Also, the starting price factors in the delayed opportunity for myself to start trying to breed with both parents having the trait. Bottomline: I’m unlikely to sell her at a lower price point right now, but given that no one beats me to the punch, I’d be happy to either try and breed a mule with the trait at a lower price, or to put a male (which, given a large enough herd of mares would allow you to start passing the trait very quickly) on auction in a couple of weeks.

comments.author: Aleck
comments.message: If you've successfully bred the trait, can you post the other horses - especially if one is this one's parent? That would convince me to start the bidding in earnest.

comments.author: SmeJack
comments.message: Just thought I would share some of my info here... I've been breeding rare pairs for a couple of months now and only one of them has produced a rare foal which to me says that the chance is no more or less than any none rare pair, I'm glad that you had good luck getting rares but I feel it is a case of the exception doesn't make the rule. I checked my logs for the mother that did birth a rare just to see how many she has bred "Search "Yazmeendep will probably give birth in a while!" (190 hits in 3 files)" So one pair almost 200 foals for one rare, and none of the other pairs, my observation puts a rare horse at about 1 in 300 but almost none of any of my breeding pairs have given birth to more than one this is just dividing my rares from total births

comments.author: Glynflorel
comments.message: Hi SmeJack, First of all, can you explain how it's possible Yazmeendep gave birth 190 times since the 26th of May? That is twice per day!? Secondly, could you provide more data? Exactly which horses did you breed? Do you already have enough horses with rare traits to regularly breed two of the same rare traits together? Finally, I have no idea what the chance of getting a rare from non-rare-traited parents is but if we assume your number of 1 in 300, the likelihood of randomly getting exactly the same rare trait as the father twice out of only 15 breedings is extremely unlikely...

comments.author: SmeJack
comments.message: She often gives birth 4 times a day, breeding is much faster on pvp servers, yes, as I said I have many pairs of rare horses breeding. Its not unlikely, like anything rng you can get lucky and its not so unlikely to have the same rare when its the dominant category

comments.author: Glynflorel
comments.message: You claim a base probability of 1/300. If we assume that there is a probability of 1 that the random rare trait assigned will be a draft trait, that still leaves two possible draft traits, lowering the probability to 1/600 per trial. For 2 out of 15 trials, that leaves us with a cumulative binomial probability of 0.00028748514. That’s extremely far from being “not unlikely”. It’s much more likely that the breeding of rare traits has been tweaked on PvP to account for the faster breeding rates.

comments.author: SmeJack
comments.message: Theres nothing to suggest that it was made different between servers but that's ok I didn't want to get into an argument, we just thought it would be remiss to not share the info

comments.author: Glynflorel
comments.message: No worries, sorry if I'm combative - my only other auction also ended out in an argument (over if beehives worked or not), which left a bad taste. It's totally fair to add your own perspective. I'm personally still convinced that with the numbers I've personally seen, it must be more likely to pass on the rare traits on PvE (0.00028748514 is really too small to just be luck, especially given that there seem to be no other clear numbers coming from PvE servers yet(?)). But I'm willing to cancel the auction until I've been able to test more and/or we've seen the effects of the upcoming patch. I don't want to rip anyone off. @Keridwyn@AleckWould you prefer that?

comments.author: Aleck
comments.message: I think that would be my preference, but I can't speak for Keridwyn. I would also love to test out breeding the horse myself, however, so just in case Keridwyn doesn't agree: 17s If Keridwyn agrees, however, I'd be fine withdrawing both our bids to await the results of further testing. Edited August 26, 2021 by Aleck

comments.author: Calan
comments.message: Unfortunately it's time to move on. Rather than letting the upkeep run out and my lovely settlement decay and be scavenged away, I thought someone might be interested in taking it over (giving me a full purse should I ever decide to return). The deed: Is 32 x 62 with upkeep at just under 4s Is centrally located on Cadence with boat access to both starter towns and the sea Is on the highway network with routes to both starter towns Has 30 animals pens nicely arranged in front of the mansion, all with enchanted grass Has 2x Good iron, 1x Acceptable copper, 1x Good gold, 1x Good silver, 1x Normal sandstone, and about 20x Tin veins (up to Good exposed, up to Very Good analysed) Has a bit of undeleveloped land on the southern end (kept mostly as a buffer, but it is where the Good gold vein is located) Included in the sale: Mansion with stone ground floor and timber first and second floors Spirit Castle [Courier 91] Large Magical Chest with some items from events (e.g., straw reindeer, valentines chocolates) Over 30 horses -- fwiw, about 1/2 four speed, 4x five speed -- plus a few hell horses and bison. Guard tower [50.1197 QL] attached to the manor Various furniture/tools, inc 2x beds, larder, fsb, bsbs, etc, inc rare small barrel Various resources in bins/chests, inc a few rares, like gold ore fragment (21/26), green apple, camelia; a supreme cherries; and over 100 oakenwood sprouts Starting bid: 25s Increment (minimum): 1s Reserve: No Buyout: 50s Sniper Protection: 1 hour Private Bids: Accepted (if you PM a private bid, I’ll post here with the date, time and amount of your bidI'll post that one's been made here with the date, time and amount) Imgur of settlement billboard, pictures taken just before today's start of winter, and deed planner with/without trees/shrubs. auctions.title: How to post or bid in an Auction - format, suggestions and netiquette
auctions.author: Davih

comments.author: Davih
comments.message: I decided to make a simple guide since there are a lot of new players that have no clues and i received (for some reason) a lot of PM from people asking me for suggestions. So i can link this thread to them (in case you want to lock it) or if you want to pin it up, even better, your call. (feel free to edit it, i might also add more informations as they come to my mind or from other people's feedback) -------------------------------------------------------------------- An auction should generally have this format: Starting bid : 5s increments : 1s reserve: 15s buyout: 30s sniper protection :1 hour no private bids [additional informations on the items, pickup/delivery informations, special rules of the auction (multi-auction) or anything else that helps clarify anything that could not be clear] (see timer thread for infos on how to create one) [image of the item, optional, either here on before everything]Starting bid : [pretty simple- what the auction starts at](min) increments : [What is the minimum increase over the previous bid. I.e. 1s means that if the highest offer is 5.5s, you must at least offer 6.5s, you can still offer anything you want above that]Reserve : [You can either specify a price, or write "hidden". That means that you reserve not to sell the item if reserve price isn't met, if it's hidden, and the auction reaches the hidden reserve, you might edit it and write that reserve is "met" instead of hidden, it's generallly a bad idea to use hidden reserves (see below)]Sniper protection: [this is a very important part of an auction, often underrated, it is written in minutes, or hours, and it works like this: in an example where the sniper protection is 30 minutes, and there are only a few minutes left, or even 28 minutes left on the auction, and a bid is made, the auction automatically extends to end 30 minutes after that offer, if someone makes another offer, the auction gets extended again to end 30 minutes after that last offer. until no offer has been made for 30 entire minutes, at that point, the auction ends. Any new bidder can join in, unless you care to specify otherwise. Usually, the lenght of the sniper protection is proportionate to the value of the item.Buyout: [Pretty simple concept, a buyout price is a price that allows you to automatically end the auction and purchase the item directly, if an offer that meets or exceeds buyout is made, then the auction is over]Private bids: [You should specify if you accept private bids or not, a private bid means that you would just trust the fact that the seller received an anonymous bid from someone that doesn't want to apper in the auction, and he will post it himself, it's usually a frown-upon feature that could be used to simply used to counter-offer your own auction, most people don't accept them] Suggestions / netiquette.- Retracting.an offer is something that should generally never be done, a bid on an item is serious matter in which you are putting your reputation as a player/buyer, if you need to retract an offer, you should provide a serious reason, and it's usually very bad manners to just retract your offer because you changed your mind or found something better or cheaper on the market while the auction was running. - Auction lenght shouldn't generally be too long - it's usually 2-3 days, longer auctions usually draw less attention or get forgotten, they might be used for particularly niche or valuable item, or maybe deeds, but it's usually best to not go over 3 days, very short auctions are also risky, you usually want at least a 24-hour timer so that people from all time zones at least have a chance to see your auction - Editing/Extending should only be used in certain situations, editing the title, fixing errors is commonly accepted, so is adding a sniper protection halfway through the auction, or even lowering the starting bid if nobody offered yet. changing things like adding a buyout or extending the timer is a case-by-case situation, but it's usually best to avoid doing so. Extending the timer just because the auction didn't reach the price that you wanted, is most likely a shady move, if the timer breaks(happens sometimes) and it's unclear when the auction is ending, it's different, and might be tolerated. adding a buyout or accepting one even though none was specified, is also a pretty bad move, even more if the buyout is proposed ingame (it could just as likely be the owner that faked a buyout to close the auction that wasn't going as good as he hoped)- Hidden reserves are something that is best avoided, not because you're cheating other people with not selling the item after all, but because you're most likely not going to get many offers on them, as people hate them and usually don't even bother to offer anything on those, furthermore decreasing the perceived value of the item that you were trying to auction, you can still use them, but as an experienced trader i strongly suggest you against it.- Making offers lower than starting bid is something that people sometimes do, it could be either trolling (if the offer is significantly lower than the starting bid) or someone that thinks that you overpriced your item and is offering what he thinks would be an acceptable offer, it's your call if you want to accept them or not, but you should generally refrain from doing offers way lower than the starting bid.- Comments in other's people auctions can be fun, and are sometimes accepted, if they are friendly, or suggestions, but they also make the auction "less readable" so you shouldn't go on too long and start chatting on an auction, negative comments are instead a very bad habit that shouldn't be taking place on auctions (and will probably be moderated) if you disagree with someone's price and really can't keep it for yourself, you should preferably PM the guy or at least stop at the first signs that your comments are not appreciated.- Refusing to conclude the trade is also, obviously, bad behaviour that will, or should impact negatively on your reputation, if you win an auction you are pretty much "forced" to buy the item for the amount you offered,.Haggling, not answering in 1-2days, or plainly refusing to fulfill the trade should be avoided at all cost, and you will be pretty much subjected to how seriously the seller wants to take your motivations, some might just shrug it off or try to find some middle ground, some other might never want to deal with you again or even go as far as publicly shaming you (which is not forbidden, if made in the right way and staying in the ingame-context), so yeah, just don't do that. - Tracking sniper protection is not automatic, but the best way to do it is to check the post with the last offer, it usually has a string written above saying "posted x minutes/hours ago" just refresh the page to have it updated , In case you weren't checking, If you mouseover it, it also says the time it was posted at, so you can just check if at any point 2 offers were made apart for more minutes than the sniper protection is, in that case, they will not count. Being flexible in accepting offers that were posted a few minutes later is not a "kindness" that you do to a guy coming in late, it will most likely be seen as bad behaviour and lack of seriousness, and should be avoided. Feel free to ask questions or give me your opinion if i missed or misinterpreted something that you feel should be different. Edited September 7, 2020 by Davih
